rationale: The workflow's single check job has no explicit timeout, so a hung or runaway Snyk scan can consume unbounded runner time. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (evidence: experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) supports bounding jobs with a custom timeout; its measured example added timeout-minutes: 5 and cut median elapsed time by ~26.8% while preserving all checks. Repository history shows five successful runs of roughly 33-43 seconds, so a 5-minute budget gives ample headroom and will not interrupt valid scans. The change adds only timeout-minutes: 5 to the existing job, preserves every step and required check, adds no permissions, secrets, network access, or publishing/deployment operations, and the workflow already uses concurrency cancel-in-progress (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE), so no conflicting change is needed.
